rule.BASELINE_DEVIATION: Deviation from your cat's own baseline

REPEATED_OUT_OF_RANGE.message: Repeated readings — In the last {{windowHours}} hours, this cat had {{n}} readings outside the 6.3–6.6 reference range, all leaning the same way. One off reading usually means little, but a repeat is worth a closer look. You can check that your cat is drinking enough, whether the food changed recently, and scan 1–2 more times tomorrow. This is an observation from litter color, not a diagnosis. If your cat strains to pee, stops eating or cries when using the litter box, take them to a vet.

BASELINE_DEVIATION.message: Different from usual — Today's reading for this cat is {{ph}}, which differs by {{delta}} from their usual level ({{baseline}}). Every cat has its own baseline, so a change compared with the same cat is usually more telling than a comparison with the general average. Note whether the food, litter or home changed recently or anything stressed your cat, and scan again in 12–24 hours to see if the reading returns to its usual level. This is an observation from litter color, not a diagnosis.

MONOTONIC_TREND.message: A trend to watch — This cat's latest scans ({{phSeries}}) are gradually shifting in one direction. A trend usually means more than a single number because it is less affected by the conditions of each photo. Try scanning once a day for the next 3 days to see if the trend continues. If you recently changed food, note down when. This is an observation from litter color, not a diagnosis.

LOW_QUALITY_STREAK.message: Tips for better scans — {{n}} recent scans had low confidence. Try placing the reference color card inside the frame, holding the camera 15–25 cm from the litter, using white light, and keeping your shadow off the litter.

URGENT_CLINICAL_SIGN.message: ⚠️ Please take your cat to a vet today. You reported signs that should not be monitored at home. In cats, straining to pee or being unable to pee can become dangerous very quickly, within a day. Do this now: call the nearest vet clinic and describe exactly what you observed. Do not wait for the next scan or until tomorrow. CatCheck only helps track litter color and cannot assess this situation. This information does not replace a veterinary examination.
